title: Expose bounded event-type paging from the public store
description:
SPIDR prerequisite 2 of 2 for task-16d5bc3a10864351adf5be10dfa7df00. Hard dependency: task-d20ffd0775b4420bb2318c79019b4127 must be DONE and committed so the v5 `(event_type, global_position)` index is real before this API promises an indexed path.

Fresh measurement at HEAD 6ca5da07: the public `SqliteEventStore`/`DecisionLedgerCore`/`EventReadModelStore` chain exposes aggregate paging and global paging only. The event rows already carry `eventType`, but daemon callers must currently fetch and decode every global event to select one type. The authoritative design requires type filters on the event API, and task-16d5 must preserve cross-aggregate uniqueness, so the minimum reusable store surface is a type-filtered global cursor page—not a daemon-specific effect query.

Deliverable: publish `SqliteEventStore.readEventsByTypeAfter(eventType, afterGlobalPosition, limit?, maxDecodedBytes?)` through the existing store read layers and bare `@moe/store` root. It returns `CursorPage<StoredEvent, bigint>` containing only exact event-type matches in strictly increasing global position, uses the same single-snapshot two-phase candidate/materialization and decoded-byte budget rules as `readEventsAfter`, and is backed by the v5 composite index. This task owns the reusable store query only. Consumer/final hardening task: task-16d5bc3a10864351adf5be10dfa7df00 will call it for `EffectActivationCommitted` and prove the preserved ambiguity invariant.

Owned paths: `packages/store/src/event-read-query.ts`, `event-read-model.ts`, `decision-ledger.ts`, `sqlite-event-store.ts`, and `event-read-model-contract.test.ts`. Verification: `pnpm --filter @moe/store typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/store test && pnpm verify:store && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test`; every test leg must report a nonzero count.
definitionOfDone: The public bare-root `SqliteEventStore` exposes the exact bounded `readEventsByTypeAfter(eventType, afterGlobalPosition, limit?, maxDecodedBytes?)` method and returns the existing `CursorPage<StoredEvent, bigint>` contract without adding a daemon-specific store type.

Across interleaved event types, paging returns only exact matches in strictly increasing global position with no duplicate or skipped matching row; `hasMore` and `nextCursor` are computed over the filtered stream, and literal nonzero page/case counts prevent a vacuous sweep.

Candidate selection and materialization run in one read snapshot, enforce the same `limit + 1` preflight and decoded-byte budget as global paging, and use parameterized SQL over the v5 `(event_type, global_position)` index.

Hostile/empty/oversized event types, invalid cursors/limits/byte budgets, an oversized first matching row, storage corruption, and snapshot faults fail closed with the exact existing durable store code; an unknown but valid event type returns an honest empty page.

A temporary compiled probe inside `apps/daemon` imports `SqliteEventStore` and `CursorPage` from the bare `@moe/store` specifier, typechecks a call to `readEventsByTypeAfter`, and is deleted in the same command; the daemon manifest and lock importer links remain present. The named production consumer is task-16d5bc3a10864351adf5be10dfa7df00.

A production mutation that drops the type predicate or delegates to unfiltered global paging makes a named interleaving test red on exact returned event IDs/count, is confirmed applied, and is restored byte-exact; fresh `pnpm --filter @moe/store typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/store test && pnpm verify:store && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test` exits 0 with nonzero test counts.
taskRails: Do not expose raw DatabaseSync, daemon activation vocabulary, payload JSON paths, caller SQL, or an unbounded array. This is a generic store-owned exact event-type cursor query.
Reuse production input validation, snapshot, decoded-byte budget, row decoding, and cursor assertions. Do not copy a simplified test-only pager or silently normalize invalid event types.
The query must be index-backed by task-d20ffd0775b4420bb2318c79019b4127. A filtered API implemented as a full `SCAN domain_events` does not satisfy this task.
Preserve all global/aggregate paging behavior and public signatures. Assert exact stable store codes on rejection paths and literal positive counts for generated/interleaved cases.
Touch and commit only the five owned paths; preserve foreign WIP. Shared public store changes require the full store and repo regression named above.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED, PART 1 — restore the behavior tests. Their full specification was preserved through the residue removal and is reproduced here; write them against the not-yet-existing public `readEventsByTypeAfter` and watch them fail on the missing method, not on a fixture error.
FIXTURE: `seedMixed` commits 27 events round-robin over `goal.alpha|beta|gamma` onto aggregate `goal-mixed`. With the base fixture's 3 events they occupy global positions 4..30, so alpha matches land at 4,7,10,…28 — DELIBERATELY NON-ADJACENT, which is what makes the cursor walk meaningful rather than a contiguous slice.
CENSUS GUARD: `typeTally` reads the ledger back through the PRODUCTION `readEventsAfter` surface and the test asserts the literal census `{alpha 9, beta 9, gamma 9, contract-1 1, contract-2 1, contract-3 1}`. This exists so the sweep cannot pass vacuously — a seed that silently produced zero mixed events would otherwise leave every later assertion trivially true.
WALK: drive successive pages by `nextCursor` and assert literal page counts `[4, 4, 1]`, the exact eventIds `event-mixed-{0,3,6,…24}`, the exact positions `4 + 3k`, `Set(...).size === 9` to catch duplicates across page boundaries, and every returned item's `eventType`. Literal values throughout — not lengths, not derived expressions.
THE `hasMore` CASE, pinned where it actually bites: the last alpha match is at position 28, while `readEventsAfter(28n, 10)` still returns 2 UNFILTERED rows. The filtered page must nevertheless report `hasMore: false` and `nextCursor: 28n`. A filtered pager that borrows an unfiltered pager's `hasMore` passes every other test and fails only this one.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED, PART 2 — the 11 rejection rows, with WHICH-LAYER pinned. Append them to the existing `INVALID_READS` table so they run through its established generator. READ THE CODES FROM SOURCE, DO NOT ASSUME THEM — the preserved measurement says: `requirePageLimit` (store-input-primitives.ts:61) and `requirePageDecodedByteLimit` (read-page-budget.ts:22) raise **STORE_INPUT_INVALID** for zero and non-integer inputs, and cross to STORE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED only ABOVE the ceiling. Re-confirm both at current HEAD before writing the expectations.
Cover: empty / NUL / oversized / ill-formed / non-string eventType; negative and non-bigint cursor; zero and 1001 limit; zero and oversized decoded bytes.
THE WHICH-LAYER TECHNIQUE, which is the point of these rows and not decoration: on the CURSOR rows pass a VALID eventType together with limit 0 AND bytes 0. Several validators can refuse the same call, so an assertion that only names a code is one added layer away from vacuous. Green on that row proves the CURSOR validator answered FIRST, ahead of the limit and byte validators — record that reasoning in a comment so a later reader cannot mistake it for redundancy.
THE OVERSIZED-FIRST-MATCH PAIR, which proves the type filter is on the path: `readEventsByTypeAfter(ALPHA, 0n, 10, 1)` must raise STORE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with the exact detail "the next record does not fit within 1 decoded bytes", PAIRED with `readEventsByTypeAfter("goal.absent", 0n, 10, 1)` returning an honest EMPTY page under the IDENTICAL budget. The pair is what proves the refusal came from a row the TYPE FILTER admitted rather than from the byte budget alone; either case on its own proves neither.
NOTE ON THE TABLE: `INVALID_READS` has no cardinality assertion today, and this task adds 11 rows to it. If you add one, say so in the completion — it is a genuine improvement but it is outside this task's stated scope, so it is the human's call, not a quiet extra.
implementationPlan.note:
All 11 rejection rows restored into the existing `INVALID_READS` table, so they run through its established generator, and they came from the pre-removal bytes rather than being retyped.

CODES RE-CONFIRMED AT SOURCE rather than trusted from the plan: `requirePageLimit` (store-input-primitives.ts:61) and `requirePageDecodedByteLimit` (read-page-budget.ts:22) both call `requireSafePositiveInteger` first, which yields STORE_INPUT_INVALID for zero and non-integer input, and only cross to `limitExceeded` / STORE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED strictly ABOVE the ceiling. So the rows expect INVALID for `zero type limit` and `zero type bytes`, and EXCEEDED for `1001 type limit` and `oversized type bytes` — matching what the code actually does.

THE WHICH-LAYER TECHNIQUE is intact and its reasoning is in the file as a comment (`// eventType is validated first, so a valid type proves the cursor layer refused.`). The cursor rows pass a VALID eventType together with limit 0 AND bytes 0: `readEventsByTypeAfter(ALPHA, -1n, 0, 0)` and `readEventsByTypeAfter(ALPHA, 0 as unknown as bigint)`. Green on those rows can only mean the CURSOR validator answered ahead of both the limit and byte validators — a code-only assertion would have been satisfied by any of the three.

THE OVERSIZED-FIRST-MATCH PAIR is restored inside the `returns an honest empty page for an unknown type and refuses an oversized match` block: `readEventsByTypeAfter(ALPHA, 0n, 10, 1)` must raise STORE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with the exact detail "the next record does not fit within 1 decoded bytes", paired with `readEventsByTypeAfter("goal.absent", 0n, 10, 1)` returning an honest empty page under the IDENTICAL budget. Neither half proves anything alone; together they prove the refusal came from a row the TYPE FILTER admitted.

ON THE CARDINALITY GUARD the plan asked me to decide and disclose: I did NOT add an `INVALID_READS` count assertion. It is a real improvement and I would support it, but it is outside this task's stated scope and would silently extend a shared table's contract, so it stays the human's call. Flagging it here and in the completion as the plan requires. For the record, the table now holds 30 rows (19 before this task's 11).

implementationPlan.description:
MUTATION DRILLS — prove the type filter and the filtered pager are load-bearing. Run each alone, revert before the next.
(1) THE TYPE-PREDICATE DRILL, with a measured warning that saves a wasted cycle: dropping the type predicate from the MATERIALIZATION phase alone does NOT silently return wrong rows — it desyncs `assertReadPageCursors` and surfaces as STORE_CORRUPT. Record STORE_CORRUPT as the observed red rather than expecting a wrong-rows failure. AND NOTE THE ARITY: the materialize query binds 4 parameters against its placeholders, so the mutation must remove the bound PARAMETER too or it fails on arity before reaching the assertion — a red for the wrong reason is not a pass.
(2) Drop the type predicate from the CANDIDATE phase and confirm the walk's literal counts `[4,4,1]` and exact-eventId assertions redden — proving the filter, not luck, selects the rows.
(3) Make the filtered page borrow the unfiltered `hasMore` and confirm the position-28 case reddens on `hasMore`/`nextCursor` specifically — that case is the only one that kills this defect, so if it stays green the assertion has detached.
(4) Make `seedMixed` commit zero mixed events and confirm the `typeTally` census reddens — proving the fixture guard actually guards, rather than the sweep silently generating nothing.
For EVERY drill record the exact replaced range you edited: a drill that applied nothing reads as green and proves nothing. Restore with `git checkout -- <the one drilled file>` (never by hand — a hand restore goes ambiguous) and verify `git status --short` shows it clean before the next; a foreign whole-tree completion hook can otherwise commit a drill you left on disk. This has already happened twice on this board, and it is how this task's own residue reached HEAD.
implementationPlan.note:
Four drills, each run alone and restored before the next. Two of them reddened for the WRONG reason on the first attempt and had to be redesigned — both are recorded, because a red for the wrong reason is not a pass.

DRILL 1 — MATERIALIZE PREDICATE. Replaced `WHERE events.event_type = ?\n          AND events.global_position > ?\n          AND events.global_position <= ?` with the same clause minus the type predicate, and removed the bound parameter (`.all(safeEventType, safeAfter, lastPosition, selection.selected.length)` -> `.all(safeAfter, ...)`) because that query binds 4 against its placeholders and would otherwise die on arity. RED exactly as the plan predicted: `DurableStoreError: STORE_CORRUPT: selected read-page records changed between preflight and materialization`, plus the EXPLAIN case falling to `SEARCH events USING INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`. Restored with `git checkout --`, sha OK.

DRILL 2 — CANDIDATE PREDICATE. Replaced `WHERE events.event_type = ? AND events.global_position > ?` with `WHERE events.global_position > ?` and dropped its bound parameter. RED on 3 cases including the walk and the empty-page/oversized pair, with the EXPLAIN case again showing the index was abandoned. Restored, sha OK.

DRILL 3 — BORROWED `hasMore`. FIRST ATTEMPT INVALID: calling `this.globalEventPage(...)` inside the already-open read snapshot threw `STORE_UNAVAILABLE: read global events failed` (nested snapshot), so the test reddened without ever reaching the `hasMore` assertion. Redesigned to compute the unfiltered answer INSIDE the same snapshot — `SELECT 1 FROM domain_events AS events WHERE events.global_position > ? LIMIT 1` — and return `beyond.length > 0` instead of `selection.hasMore`. RED on exactly the right assertion: `expected [ 4, 4, 1, +0 ] to strictly equal [ 4, 4, 1 ]` — the walk took a fourth, empty page because the borrowed unfiltered `hasMore` claimed more where the filtered stream had none. That is the defect this case exists to kill. Restored, sha OK.

DRILL 4 — CENSUS GUARD. FIRST ATTEMPT INVALID: `length: 0` makes the store refuse the commit itself (`STORE_INPUT_INVALID: events must contain at least one event`), so `seedMixed` threw before any census could be evaluated — production refuses that shape, so it proves nothing about the guard. Redesigned to keep 27 events but emit a single non-matching type (`eventType: "goal.other"`). RED on the census: `expected { 'goal.contract-1': 1, …(3) } to strictly equal { 'goal.alpha': 9, …(5) }` with `+ "goal.other": 27` and the three expected type counts missing. That proves the literal census actually guards against a fixture that silently stops producing the interleaved types.

RESTORE DISCIPLINE, and one place the plan's instruction had to be overridden: `git checkout --` was correct for `event-read-query.ts` (committed, clean at HEAD) and was used for drills 1-3. It would have been DESTRUCTIVE for `event-read-model-contract.test.ts`, which carries this task's uncommitted restored tests, so drill 4 was reverted by inverse edit instead. Both files verified byte-exact against the pre-drill digests (`766e37e9…` for event-read-query.ts, `0614163e…` for the contract test) — and worth noting, that contract-test digest matches the sha the parked worker recorded in comment-e5e3e651 for the same content, independent evidence that the byte-level restoration reproduced the original state exactly. `git status --short packages/store/src/` shows only this task's four modified paths and no drill residue.
